transformations.edit: Extracted the target-local RChunksExact representation with private `v`, `rem`, and `chunk_size` fields, preserving field names, order, types, and privacy while omitting Rust stability/doc attributes.
Included RChunksExact::new with the real Rust body order: `let rem = slice.len() % chunk_size; let (fst, snd) = ...; Self { v: snd, rem: fst, chunk_size }`.

Adapted the helper's `unsafe { slice.split_at_unchecked(rem) }` to the reviewed vstd `slice.split_at(rem)` contract after proving `rem <= slice.len()`; this exposes the same prefix/suffix data flow at the valid index and is recorded as a minimal split boundary.
Adapted the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &[T]` parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains assert then RChunksExact::new(slice, chunk_size).
Adapted the Rust `pub const fn` target item to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Adapted the private Rust `pub(super) const fn` constructor to a non-const Verus harness function; no executable control-flow or data-flow step was changed.
Converted Rust `assert!(chunk_size != 0, ...)` to Verus `assert(chunk_size != 0)` under the same generated precondition; no control-flow path is removed.

Defined the closed iterator-view helper from the extracted `rem`, `v`, and `chunk_size` fields to expose source as `rem + v`, remaining as `v`, empty yielded prefix, prefix remainder, requested chunk size, and reverse direction.

Inlined the generated shared vocabulary predicates `slice_iterator_well_formed` and `slice_chunk_partition` so Verus can check the exact reverse-partition postcondition against the source-backed iterator view.

Added proof-only arithmetic, sequence-split, and reveal annotations to discharge `rem < chunk_size`, divisibility of the suffix partition, and prefix/suffix recomposition; these have no executable data-flow or evaluation-order effect.
